text: Are there any E. coli expression studies about ciprofloxacin?

## Abstract

Yes. A targeted search of NCBI GEO for *Escherichia coli* Series records containing “ciprofloxacin” returned 37 expression-study records, although this broad metadata query includes studies where ciprofloxacin is contextual rather than a direct transcriptional perturbation. A parallel NIAID Data Ecosystem (NDE) dataset search returned 110 matching Dataset records, including duplicated representations of the same BioProjects, GEO Series, and SRA studies. I retrieved detailed GEO metadata for seven directly relevant studies spanning 2015–2025. These include four RNA-seq studies, two microarray studies, and one mixed-species RNA-seq comparison. Their deposited sample totals range from 4 to 42 per Series. The studies cover ciprofloxacin exposure in *E. coli* K-12 MG1655, multidrug-resistant ST131, enteropathogenic *E. coli*, and an unspecified *E. coli* record. Designs include early time-course exposure, high-dose exposure, glutathione co-treatment, comparison of wild type with a Δ*purA* mutant, and comparison with GuaB inhibition. Processed expression data are available as GEO supplementary files for all seven retrieved Series. These records provide a practical starting set for comparative analyses of the ciprofloxacin transcriptional response, including SOS/DNA-damage responses, respiratory and metabolic state, and antibiotic-tolerance mechanisms.

## I. Introduction

**Background.** Ciprofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone antibiotic. Expression profiling in *E. coli* can identify transcriptional programs associated with acute drug exposure, DNA damage, tolerance, and drug-modifying co-treatments.

**Literature Review.** Retrieved PubMed-linked records include studies of ciprofloxacin resistance reversal in *E. coli* K-12 (PMID 30013537), glutathione–ciprofloxacin transcriptional responses (PMID 29468195), early antibiotic-exposure transcriptomics (PMID 41805196), and quinolone tolerance associated with de novo adenosine-ribonucleotide biosynthesis defects (PMID 42079445).

**Knowledge Gap.** It was unclear whether public *E. coli* expression datasets specifically included ciprofloxacin exposure and whether their processed expression data were accessible.

**Objective & Hypothesis.** The objective was to identify public *E. coli* expression studies about ciprofloxacin. The expectation was that GEO would contain directly relevant RNA-seq and microarray Series with downloadable processed data.

## II. Materials and Methods

**Study Design.** GEO was selected to identify transcriptomic and microarray Series and to obtain study-level metadata and supplementary-file locations. NDE was queried in parallel to identify related federated records across GEO, BioProject, and SRA. PubMed summaries were retrieved only for PubMed IDs linked by GEO.

**Materials.**

- NCBI GEO, accessed with `geo_search` and `geo_series`.
- NIAID Data Ecosystem, accessed with `nde_search_datasets`.
- PubMed, accessed with `pubmed_get_summaries`.

**Procedures.**

1. `geo_search(organism="Escherichia coli", term="ciprofloxacin", entry_type="gse", max_results=20)`.
2. `nde_search_datasets(query="Escherichia coli ciprofloxacin expression", record_type="Dataset", size=20, sort="relevance")`.
3. Detailed GEO retrievals, each with `list_files=true`:
   - `geo_series(accession="GSE89507", list_files=true)`
   - `geo_series(accession="GSE93896", list_files=true)`
   - `geo_series(accession="GSE75988", list_files=true)`
   - `geo_series(accession="GSE295494", list_files=true)`
   - `geo_series(accession="GSE292923", list_files=true)`
   - `geo_series(accession="GSE152445", list_files=true)`
   - `geo_series(accession="GSE275261", list_files=true)`
4. `pubmed_get_summaries(pmids=["30013537","29468195","41805196","42079445"])`.

**Statistical Analysis.** The GEO search’s total of 37 is the `total_count` from the GEO Series query after NCBI query translation. The NDE total of 110 is the number of federated Dataset records returned by its query and is not deduplicated across repositories. The focused table contains seven manually screened GEO Series whose titles, summaries, or sample labels explicitly describe ciprofloxacin exposure or ciprofloxacin-related transcriptional comparison. Sample counts are the `sample_count` fields for each GEO Series; they represent all samples in a Series, including controls and non-ciprofloxacin comparator arms where applicable.

## III. Results

**Data Presentation.**

**Table 1. Directly relevant *E. coli* ciprofloxacin expression Series retrieved from GEO.**

| GEO Series | Organism / strain | Platform / assay | Deposited samples | Ciprofloxacin-related design | Processed-data availability |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| GSE75988 | *Escherichia coli*; enteropathogenic *E. coli* in title | Microarray | 15 | Transcriptional response after ciprofloxacin exposure; sample labels include 0, 45, 90, 135, and 180 min | GEO RAW archive |
| GSE89507 | *E. coli* O25b:H4-ST131 | RNA-seq | 6 | 2 µg/mL ciprofloxacin; 0, 30, and 90 min samples with and without drug | Per-timepoint TXT and XML files |
| GSE93896 | *E. coli* K-12 MG1655 | Microarray | 8 | Control, glutathione, ciprofloxacin at 3 ng/mL, and glutathione plus ciprofloxacin at 50 ng/mL | RAW archive and compressed XLS data |
| GSE152445 | *E. coli* K-12 MG1655 | RNA-seq | 6 | High-dose ciprofloxacin study; sample labels include untreated and 2 µg conditions | FPKM matrix |
| GSE275261 | *E. coli* and *Acinetobacter baumannii* | RNA-seq | 24 | Includes *E. coli* ciprofloxacin, no-drug, and GuaB-inhibitor conditions at 1 h | *E. coli* count matrix and metadata |
| GSE292923 | *E. coli* | RNA-seq | 4 | Wild type and Δ*purA*, sampled at 0 and 90 min during ciprofloxacin treatment | Four differential-expression result files |
| GSE295494 | *E. coli* K-12 MG1655 | RNA-seq | 42 | Early ciprofloxacin-response time course; cipro-labelled samples span 0–30 min, with additional antibiotic conditions | Raw-count matrix |

**Findings.**

- The broad GEO Series search reported **37** *E. coli*–ciprofloxacin records.
- The NDE federated Dataset search reported **110** records. This is not directly comparable with the GEO count because NDE includes duplicate representations of datasets across GEO, BioProject, and SRA.
- Seven GEO Series were retrieved in detail as direct ciprofloxacin-expression studies.
- Four of seven Series use high-throughput sequencing, two use array-based expression profiling, and one high-throughput Series contains both *E. coli* and *A. baumannii*.
- All seven Series list supplementary files containing either processed expression matrices, raw counts, sample metadata, or differential-expression tables.
- Four focused Series have GEO-linked PubMed IDs: GSE89507, GSE93896, GSE295494, and GSE292923.
- GSE75988 and GSE152445 have no PubMed link registered in GEO.

## IV. Discussion

**Interpretation.** Public data exist for the requested topic. The seven screened Series provide directly usable starting points for ciprofloxacin-response analyses in *E. coli*. GSE295494 is suited to short-timescale responses, GSE89507 to a clinically relevant multidrug-resistant ST131 strain, GSE93896 to a glutathione co-treatment design, GSE292923 to a Δ*purA* tolerance mechanism, and GSE152445 to high-dose ciprofloxacin exposure.

**Context.** The retrieved literature aligns with the dataset designs. PMID 30013537 addresses ciprofloxacin resistance reversal and corresponds to GSE89507. PMID 29468195 concerns glutathione and ciprofloxacin and corresponds to GSE93896. PMID 41805196 corresponds to the early-exposure time-course dataset GSE295494. PMID 42079445 corresponds to the Δ*purA* ciprofloxacin-tolerance dataset GSE292923.

**Limitations.** The broad GEO search count was generated after NCBI’s automated query translation and can include records that mention ciprofloxacin without measuring a direct ciprofloxacin transcriptional response. GEO API metadata do not contain the expression matrices; the data reside in supplementary files and must be downloaded separately. The NDE count includes federated duplicates and therefore should not be interpreted as a count of distinct biological studies. Sample totals for mixed-condition Series are not counts of ciprofloxacin-treated samples alone.

**Conclusion & Future Directions.** Yes—there are multiple public *E. coli* expression studies involving ciprofloxacin, including RNA-seq and microarray designs from 2015 through 2025. A next query should retrieve raw sequencing runs for a selected BioProject, such as PRJNA352402, PRJNA639434, PRJNA1241879, or PRJNA1254960, or download and harmonize the processed matrices from the GEO supplementary files. A downloadable TSV/CSV table of the screened studies can be generated on request.

## References

[1] NCBI GEO, GEO Series search provenance: https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi

[2] NIAID Data Ecosystem, dataset-search provenance: https://api.data.niaid.nih.gov/v1/query?q=%28Escherichia+coli+ciprofloxacin+expression%29+AND+%40type%3A%22Dataset%22&size=20&_source=_id%2C%40type%2Cname%2Cdescription%2Curl%2Cdoi%2Cidentifier%2Cdate%2CdatePublished%2CdateModified%2CincludedInDataCatalog.name%2CincludedInDataCatalog.url%2CincludedInDataCatalog.archivedAt%2Cauthor.name%2CinfectionsAgent.name%2CinfectionsAgent.displayName%2Cspecies.name%2ChealthCondition.name%2CmeasurementTechnique.name%2CtopicCategory.name%2Ckeywords%2CconditionsOfAccess%2Clicense%2Cdistribution.contentUrl%2CsourceOrganization.name%2Cfunding.funder.name%2CprogrammingLanguage%2CapplicationCategory%2CoperatingSystem%2CsoftwareVersion%2CcodeRepository%2CisBasedOn.identifier%2CvariableMeasured.name%2Cvalue%2CunitText%2CmarginOfError.name%2CmarginOfError.value%2CobservationAbout.name%2CobservationAbout.identifier%2CmeasuredProperty.name%2CobservationType.name%2CmeasurementQualifier%2CsubjectOf.identifier

[3] NCBI GEO, GSE75988 record: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE75988

[4] NCBI GEO, GSE89507 record: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE89507

[5] NCBI GEO, GSE93896 record: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE93896

[6] NCBI GEO, GSE152445 record: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE152445

[7] NCBI GEO, GSE275261 record: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE275261

[8] NCBI GEO, GSE292923 record: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE292923

[9] NCBI GEO, GSE295494 record: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE295494

[10] PubMed, PMID 30013537: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30013537/

[11] PubMed, PMID 29468195: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29468195/

[12] PubMed, PMID 41805196: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41805196/

[13] PubMed, PMID 42079445: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42079445/

Data providers: NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus, NCBI PubMed, and the NIAID Data Ecosystem.
